name: Light-weight 4D Gaussian Splatting (LGS)
definition: A method for efficient surgical scene reconstruction that combines Deformation-Aware Pruning (DAP), Gaussian-Attribute Pruning (GAP), and Feature Field Condensation (FFC) to reduce memory usage while maintaining high-quality real-time rendering of dynamic scenes.
summary: Light-weight 4D Gaussian Splatting is a memory-efficient method for rendering dynamic scenes that achieves significant compression and real-time speeds by pruning Gaussians and condensing feature fields.
